attacks.claim: S1's acceptance bar — 'the reviewer diffs the deleted .action* rules against ActionButton's <style> block and confirms byte equality apart from selector renaming' — is unsatisfiable for AdoptByIpRow: its `.adopt-row .action` (AdoptByIpRow.svelte:93-111) is a materially different rule set from ControllerStatusPanel's `.action` (ControllerStatusPanel.svelte:579-597): `flex: none; width: auto; padding: var(--space-1) var(--space-3)` and no `gap: 6px`, versus `flex: 1; gap: 6px; padding: var(--space-1) var(--space-2)`. Adopting the proposed ActionButton (props: onclick/disabled/wide/pressed/tone/title/ariaLabel) in AdoptByIpRow either stretches the Adopt button across the row (visible layout change on an untested surface) or requires a sized-to-label variant the plan never specifies; the jsdom anchor AdoptByIpRow.test.ts cannot detect either outcome.
attacks.evidence: AdoptByIpRow.svelte:91-111 ('Sized to its label here (auto width, wider inline padding) rather than stretching the row') vs ControllerStatusPanel.svelte:579-597 — verified by reading both style blocks at HEAD; deltas: flex none vs flex 1, width auto, space-3 vs space-2 inline padding, missing gap.
attacks.repair: Add a `fit: 'stretch' | 'label'` (or `size`) variant to ActionButton carrying the AdoptByIpRow deltas, name the visual deltas per adoption site, and restate the reviewer check as per-site rule-block equivalence against the site's OWN deleted copy — or drop AdoptByIpRow from S1's adoption set and keep its variant local.

attacks.claim: S7's visual-parity check aims at the wrong surface: the `patch-controller` preset in scripts/ui-shot/shots.json is `{state: 'view:patch', target: 'node:controller'}` — it captures the controller NODE in the patch graph, not ControllerStatusPanel, which mounts only inside OutputStatusPanel (OutputStatusPanel.svelte:115). Even if a capture reached the panel, a dev app with no live PixLite can only show the un-adopted/discovery state, so the adopted/LOST/takeover/test-pattern states that S7's split moves have zero capture coverage; the four stub-fed states already demoed in SectionComposites.svelte:385-389 (receiving, not-receiving, LOST, un-adopted) are the only reachable renderings of those branches and the plan never captures them.
attacks.evidence: scripts/ui-shot/shots.json key 'patch-controller' = {"state": "view:patch", "target": "node:controller", "settle": 1500}; grep shows ControllerStatusPanel's only app mount is OutputStatusPanel.svelte:115; SectionComposites.svelte:385-389 renders the four states on stubs.
attacks.repair: In S0 add a preset against the styleguide route (`route: '?style'`) cropping the ControllerStatusPanel demo cards in SectionComposites, and make that capture pair — not `patch-controller` — the S7 pixel-parity bar; keep patch-controller only as a smoke shot.

attacks.claim: S7 never instructs moving the parent's scoped CSS with the markup it styles. Svelte scoped styles do not reach child components: every rule in ControllerStatusPanel's <style> block that matches markup relocated into ControllerBanners/ControllerDiscovery/ControllerReadout/ControllerAuthField/ControllerTestPatterns silently stops applying after the split. The step's stated anchor (ControllerStatusPanel.test.ts byte-unmodified and green) is jsdom and cannot fail on lost styling, so an implementer following the step text to the letter can land a green commit with five visually broken sections.
attacks.evidence: S7's intent text specifies only that 'every $derived that feeds one child moves with it' — no mention of the style block; ControllerStatusPanel.svelte's <style> (lines ~560-847) contains the banner, actions, readout and test-pattern rules; Svelte scoping is per-component by construction.
attacks.repair: Add to S7: each extracted child takes the scoped rules matching its markup verbatim into its own <style>; acceptance adds `svelte-check`'s unused-selector warnings must be zero in ControllerStatusPanel after the split (Svelte emits css-unused-selector for orphaned rules), plus the styleguide-route capture from the S7 repair above.

attacks.claim: S2's acceptance ('the reviewer confirms in the diff that the four CSS rules moved verbatim into InspectorHeader') is unsatisfiable as written because the five copies are not identical: ModifierNodeInspector.svelte's `.sub` rule carries `text-transform: capitalize` that the other four sites lack. Moving one canonical block verbatim either strips capitalization from the modifier inspector's subtitle (a visible change on a zero-coverage surface) or the component needs a variant the prop list ({eyebrow, title, sub, leading, trailing}) does not express, and the step text gives the implementer no instruction either way.
attacks.evidence: grep -c 'text-transform: capitalize' across the five files: only inspectors/ModifierNodeInspector.svelte has it (its .sub block, ~line 146); jscpd in the finding likewise shows PlayNode/ModifierNode as partial 93-token matches vs the 144-token full clones.
attacks.repair: Name the canonical block (Inspector.svelte's), enumerate the two variant sites, and either add a `subTransform`/class pass-through or keep `text-transform: capitalize` at the ModifierNodeInspector call site via its own scoped selector on the sub slot — decided in the plan, not by the implementer.

attacks.claim: S0's baseline provenance is false as written: the captures are described as taken 'at the pre-change sha' and stored as `.ui-shots/baseline-3708648/`, but HEAD is already past 3708648 (fix batches 1-3: dead-code removals and the kit-mirror removal landed tonight), so the baseline is actually captured at a different sha it does not name. A later reviewer diffing against 'baseline-3708648' inherits a mislabelled reference, and dead-code batch 1 deleted whole components — captures at true 3708648 would not even match the app being changed.
attacks.evidence: Task-settled fact: fix batches 1-3 already landed on top of baseline sha 3708648; S0 verification text says 'copied to .ui-shots/baseline-3708648/' and behaviour_parity_evidence_plan.baseline_reference says 'produced by S0 at the pre-change HEAD'.
attacks.repair: Name the directory `.ui-shots/baseline-<sha-of-S0-HEAD>/` and state in S0 that the visual baseline is post-batch-1-3 HEAD, distinct from the analysis baseline 3708648.

attacks.evidence: The three call sites each call store.startMidiLearn with their own target shape (DrumZonesList.svelte:121-148, TriggerSourceInspector.svelte:180-201, PatchZoneInspector.svelte:66-88).
attacks.plan_response: S3's intent explicitly designs this out: 'The component must NOT take a learn-target descriptor: keeping store.startMidiLearn({kind, drumId, slot}) in the callers is what lets INIT-07's {drumId,slot} address-object change land without touching this component' — props are {learning, disabled, onToggle, children} only, and I verified all three sites already own their target dispatch and differ only in armed-state naming.

attacks.evidence: scripts/ui-shot/README.md:92: 'Blank-pixel detection is not yet implemented — eyeball canvas-heavy shots'; no compare/magick binary claimed by the plan.
attacks.plan_response: known_gaps (2) states exactly this ('a human eyeball, not a machine gate') and open question 6 escalates the pixelmatch-comparator decision to Trent rather than papering over it. The plan is honest about the gap; the repair is priced and offered, not hidden.

attacks.claim: S0's `styleguide-primitives` preset via `--route "?style"` may not be expressible: shots.json presets are documented as {state, target, name, viewport, settle} and a route-based preset could be unsupported, making the step unexecutable as written.
